## Key publications
- Boyle, Eugene. (2024). Investigating the Utility of the Comprehensive Trail Making Test -Second Edition (CTMT-2) in Assessing Attentional Deficits Among Children and Adolescents. Fielding Graduate University doctoral dissertation (ProQuest 31761032; N = 30, ages 8–15). CTMT-2 correlated with/predicted WISC-V Processing Speed Index and TEA-Ch2 Selective Attention and Everyday Attention indices; positioned as a supplemental tool for attentional assessment relevant to ADHD evaluation. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387076027_Investigating_the_Utility_of_the_Comprehensive_Trail_Making_Test_-Second_Edition_CTMT-2_in_Assessing_Attentional_Deficits_Among_Children_and_Adolescents
- Mizock, L., Merg, A. L., Boyle, E. J., & Kompaniez-Dunigan, E. (2019). Motherhood reimagined: Experiences of women with SMI surrounding parenting. Psychiatric Rehabilitation Journal, 42(2), 105–112. https://doi.org/10.1037/prj0000339
- Themes (2019 study): motherhood declined; motherhood derailed; motherhood disabled; motherhood reimagined; mattering through motherhood
